text: dsh-dock-attention 是一个适用于 macOS 桌面端的 DeepSeek Harness Host 插件：当会话需要用户处理而 Harness 不在前台时，它通过独立的 DSH Attention 辅助应用让 Dock 图标弹跳。插件监听审批请求、agent 提问和回合结束等事件，忽略用户取消等情况，并可跳过子 agent；用户点击提示图标会返回 Harness。提示可设置为关键或信息模式，并配置触发类型、时长、节流间隔和目标应用。首次运行会在用户 Application Support 目录安装辅助应用并写入请求及日志文件；不需要 API key 或外部账号。

dsh-dock-attention is a macOS DSH plugin that bounces a separate Dock icon for approvals, agent questions, and completed turns while Harness is in the background. Clicking it returns to Harness. No API key is needed.
DSH 在后台等我处理审批时，能不能让 Dock 图标动一下提醒我？
希望 agent 提问或一轮运行结束后，macOS 能给我一个醒目的 Dock 提示。
Can I get a bouncing Dock beacon when my background DSH session needs my attention?
dsh-dock-attention 的功能「后台会话 Dock 提醒」：检测 DSH 会话中的审批请求、用户问题和回合结束事件；当目标应用不在前台时启动辅助应用弹跳 Dock 图标，点击提示可切回 Harness，超时后提示退出。

A Host plugin for **DeepSeek Harness** that bounces a Dock icon when the agent needs
you and the Harness window is not frontmost.

dsh-dock-attention README · dsh-dock-attention：The plugin watches the durable session event feed — approvals, agent questions and
finished turns — and only then reaches for the Dock. If you are already looking at
Harness, nothing happens: attention is for when you are away, not for interrupting
the window you are in.

dsh-dock-attention README · Why a separate beacon in the Dock：The Dock tile of the Desktop app belongs to its Electron main process, and
`app.dock.bounce()` is a main-process API. A Host plugin runs in a separate Node
child process (the private Desktop Host) and cannot call it; the Dock additionally
refuses cross-process "bounce another app's tile" requests unless the caller carries
a private entitlement. That makes "make the DSH icon bounce" impossible for a plain
plugin, no matter which hook it uses.
section: Why a separate beacon in the Dock

section: Why a separate beacon in the Dock
Why a separate beacon in the Dock

text:
dsh-dock-attention README · Why a separate beacon in the Dock：Clicking the bouncing tile activates Harness (or launches it, when it is not
running). The tile has to belong to an ordinary app: a background agent
(`LSUIElement`) that promotes itself to a regular app gets a Dock tile
LaunchServices cannot reopen, so a click on it makes macOS reveal the bundle in
Finder instead of activating the app — the click never reaches the helper. Versions
before 1.0.2 worked that way and opened Finder instead of Harness; the beacon stays
a plain regular app now.
section: Why a separate beacon in the Dock

text:
dsh-dock-attention README · Why a separate beacon in the Dock：The helper is copied once to
`~/Library/Application Support/dsh-dock-attention/DSH Attention.app` (quarantine
flag stripped, ad-hoc signed, registered with LaunchServices) and launched from
there, so its Dock tile always belongs to one stable app bundle instead of a file
inside `node_modules`. The request and log files live next to it in `runtime/`;
a plugin update refreshes the copy automatically.
section: Why a separate beacon in the Dock

text:
dsh-dock-attention README · Why a separate beacon in the Dock：The helper needs **no** Accessibility, Automation, Screen Recording or Notification
permissions: focus detection uses `NSWorkspace` through JXA, and the bounce is
AppKit's own `requestUserAttention`.

text:
dsh-dock-attention README · What triggers it：| Moment | Event | Default |
|---|---|---|
| The agent waits for an approval decision | `approval/asked` | on |
| The agent asks a question (`ask_user_question`, `exit_plan_mode`) | `tool/call` | on |
| A turn finished, failed, was blocked, or hit the token limit | `turn/end` | on |

dsh-dock-attention README · What triggers it：Silent cases: turns the user cancelled (`aborted`), forked or interrupted turns, and
subagent sessions (unless `includeSubagents: true`). A bounce is also skipped when
one of `activeBundleIds` is frontmost, when a beacon is already bouncing, or when
the event arrives within `minIntervalSeconds` of the previous one.

dsh-dock-attention README · Install：**Plugin Manager / CLI:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "github:ihodorchenko/dsh-dock-attention"
```

Plugin Manager also accepts the git URL
`git+https://github.com/ihodorchenko/dsh-dock-attention.git`. A source archive is
attached to every [release](https://github.com/ihodorchenko/dsh-dock-attention/releases).

**From a local checkout:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-dock-attention"
```

The plugin only runs on macOS. On other platforms it mounts and does nothing.
dsh-dock-attention README · Configuration：Every field is optional; the row's `config` mapping is merged over these defaults.

dsh-dock-attention README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `targetBundleId` | `com.deepseek.dsh` | App the beacon activates and watches. Point it at your browser bundle id when you run `dsh web` in a browser. |
| `activeBundleIds` | `['com.deepseek.dsh']` | Foreground apps that count as "already looking at Harness". |
| `skipWhenActive` | `true` | Never bounce while one of `activeBundleIds` is frontmost. |
| `bounceOnApproval` | `true` | Bounce when an approval is requested. |
| `bounceOnQuestion` | `true` | Bounce when the agent asks a question. |
| `bounceOnTurnEnd` | `true` | Bounce when a turn ends (finished, failed, blocked, token limit). |
| `includeSubagents` | `false` | Also bounce for subagent sessions. |
| `mode` | `critical` | `critical` bounces until you come back (or the timeout); `informational` bounces `repeatCount` times. |
| `repeatCount` | `3` | Number of single bounces in `informational` mode (1–20). |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `30` | How long the beacon tile may stay in the Dock (3–300). |
| `minIntervalSeconds` | `3` | Debounce window between two bounces (0–120). |
| `sound` | `null` | macOS system

- id: dock-attention
  name: dsh-dock-attention
  config:
    mode: critical

Running `dsh web` in Safari? Use:

```yaml
config:
  targetBundleId: com.apple.Safari
  activeBundleIds: ['com.apple.Safari']
```

dsh-dock-attention README · Verifying it works：```sh
node tools/self-check.mjs
```

The self-check compiles nothing; it installs the beacon copy, launches it, watches
it through `NSWorkspace`, waits for it to exit, and prints the helper log tail. It
also prints the installed location it launched from. Watch the Dock while it runs: a
bouncing **DSH Attention** icon should appear and disappear after about eight
seconds.

dsh-dock-attention README · Limitations：- **macOS only.** The whole mechanism is macOS-specific.
- **The beacon is a separate Dock icon**, not the Harness icon itself (see
  "Why a separate beacon" above). It exists in the Dock only while attention is
  pending; clicking it returns to Harness.
- **While the beacon is active it is a regular app**, so it is visible in the Dock
  and can appear in Cmd-Tab for those few seconds. It never takes focus on launch.
- **No notification and no sound by default** — those are separate plugins. Set
  `sound` or pair it with `dsh-macos-notifications` if you want more than motion.
- macOS "Reduce motion" and third-party Dock-animation tweaks can suppress the
  bounce animation; the plugin cannot detect that. The tile still appears.
- macOS throttles very long `critical` requests; lower `timeoutSeconds` (10–15 s) if
  you want a shorter, unthrottled burst.
- The helper is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. On first use the plugin copies it to
  `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-dock-attention/` and strips the quarantine flag
  from that copy, so `git`, local-checkout and zip installs all behave the same; no
  manual `xattr` command is needed.

dsh-dock-attention README · Troubleshooting：- **No icon appears at all** — run `node tools/self-check.mjs`; it reports whether the
  helper launched at all and prints the tail of
  `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-dock-attention/runtime/helper.log`.
- **Clicking the icon opens Finder instead of Harness** — that is the pre-1.0.2
  build. It started as a background agent and promoted itself to a regular app, so
  its Dock tile could not be reopened by LaunchServices, and it also ran from inside
  the package directory. Update to 1.0.2+: the beacon is a plain regular app launched
  from a stable Application Support copy, so a click is an ordinary Dock activation.
- **Icon appears but never bounces** — check "Reduce motion" in System Settings →
  Accessibility, and Dock animation tweaks. The beacon log still shows
  `requestUserAttention(...) -> id=0`, which means the request was accepted
  (return value `0` is a valid first request id — `-1` would mean the app was active).
- **The beacon appears while you are already looking at Harness** — set

dsh-dock-attention README · Files：| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host plugin: session-event listeners and attention dispatch |
| `lib/attention.js` | Config normalization, event mapping, focus probe, beacon launch |
| `bin/DSH Attention.app` | Native beacon app (universal binary, ad-hoc signed) |
| `src/helper/main.swift` | Beacon source; `tools/build-helper.sh` rebuilds the bundle |
| `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-dock-attention/` | Installed helper copy plus `runtime/request.json` and `runtime/helper.log`, written at run time |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch that inserts the `dock-attention` row |
| `locale/en.json`, `locale/ru.json` | Plugin Manager display metadata |
| `icon.svg`, `docs/icon-1024.png` | Plugin icon and app icon source |

dsh-dock-attention README · Development：```sh
node --test                        # 23 unit tests (config, event mapping, wiring, helper bundle)
bash tools/build-helper.sh         # rebuild bin/DSH Attention.app (needs Xcode CLT)
python3 tools/render-icon.py       # optional: re-render AppIcon.icns (needs Pillow)
```

dsh-dock-attention README · Development：The helper source is small enough to audit: `requestAttention`, the single-instance
guard, the frontmost-app poll, and the click/activation forwarding are all in
`src/helper/main.swift`. Keep it a regular app: the `tests/helper.test.mjs` guard
fails if `LSUIElement` ever comes back.

dsh-dock-attention README · License：MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The beacon is ad-hoc signed (no Apple Developer
identity), so it carries no notarization; it is launched from a local package
directory and needs no quarantine escape hatch.
